questions.question: 10% of this IPO's money is an offer for sale. Where does that part of the money go?

choices.text: Into the company, to build new factories.
To the existing owners who are selling their shares.

questions.explanation: In an offer for sale, existing owners sell shares they already hold, so the money goes to them. Only the fresh issue, ₹51.01 crore here, reaches Vedant Poly Fabs Limited.

numbers.name: ofs_share
numbers.label: Share of the IPO money going to sellers

questions.question: Big institutions asked for 327.3x the shares kept for them. Why do people watch this figure?

choices.text: Professionals who studied the company closely are showing how keen they are.
It guarantees the share price will rise on listing day.
It tells you how many shares you will be given.

questions.explanation: Institutions do the most homework, and they asked for 327.3x their quota of Vedant Poly Fabs Limited: strong appetite. Still, no figure guarantees a listing gain.

numbers.name: qib_x
numbers.label: Times big institutions' shares were asked for

questions.question: An unofficial grey market premium of ₹1 a share is being quoted. How much should you rely on it?

choices.text: Completely: it tells you the listing price.
A little at most: it is unregulated and easy to push around.
It is set by the stock exchange.

questions.explanation: The grey market premium of ₹1 for Vedant Poly Fabs Limited is gossip with a number on it: nobody regulates it, and it often turns out wrong.
